reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not address residual thermal stresses, dislocation generation from cooling, or their effects on mechanical properties in HfNbTaTiZr. E1 reports tensile properties of a different alloy (NbTaHfTiZrV0.5) without discussing residual stress, and E2 is a molecular dynamics study of CrMnFeCoNi and CrFeCoNi at high strain rates, unrelated to the hypothesis. The key premises are entirely unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Thermal expansion mismatch during cooling creates residual stresses in HfNbTaTiZr.
Residual stresses generate additional dislocations and lattice distortions.
These dislocations and distortions boost yield strength and modulate elastic modulus.
These dislocations and distortions affect work-hardening during cold rolling and high-temperature creep.
Aging at 600–800 °C partially relaxes or modifies these dislocation structures.
